title: Kernel flavor orchestrator for mixed-format streaming inference
creator: Alexandra Kim
description: Objective: design and implement a runtime orchestrator that can switch between INT8 and FP8 kernel flavors at token granularity during streaming decode and prefill, minimizing dequantization overhead and preventing quality regressions. Motivation: current single-path kernel selection either pays too high a computation cost (FP8 everywhere) or incurs accuracy regressions and expensive frequent dequant (aggressive INT8). The orchestrator should allow low-latency INT8 fastpaths for most tokens while seamlessly routing to FP8 for layers/heads that materially affect output quality, and avoid repeated dequant/requant when possible.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime can decide kernel flavor per-token with <1.5ms median decision overhead on p4d-like hardware
End-to-end streaming P95 latency not increased by more than 10% for baseline workloads compared to current opt path
Token compute cost reduction >= 12% on representative chat workloads versus FP8-only baseline
Regression in output quality (ROUGE/BLEU/sampled human eval) <= 1% on monitored prompt suite
Automated telemetry shows correct kernel metrics and fallbacks; can be toggled via feature flag and rolled out to 10% -> 50% -> 100%
implementation_notes: Introduce a lightweight kernel flavor table keyed by (model, layer, head, prefetched_KV_state) to avoid global dequant decisions
Tag KV cache entries with precision metadata to enable zero-copy reuse when routing flavor differs from previous token
Implement a decision policy that considers: recent per-layer quality delta heatmap, cost delta (estimated cycles), and remaining sequence budget
Expose a tracing span per decision and emit per-token metrics to observability (console-telemetry: kernel_choice, decision_time_ms, fallback_reason)
Provide a graceful fallback: if chosen INT8 kernel reports numerical instability or kernel failure, fallback to FP8 for that microbatch and record event for analysis
benchmarks: Local microbench: gpt-medium streaming suite: INT8-favor policy reduced token CPU cycles by 18% (median) vs FP8 baseline
Cluster perf: p4d synthetic: decision overhead median 1.2ms, 95th 3.6ms (optimizations pending)
Quality eval: sample-set-of-200 prompts shows 0.6% difference in top-1 generation vs FP8 baseline (within threshold)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: oscillation between flavors causes KV churn and higher latency. Mitigation: add sticky-window heuristic (min-flavor-duration in tokens) and cache-precision pinning
Risk: numerical instability in INT8 path for specific heads. Mitigation: per-head flagging and offline head-sensitivity calibration job; immediate runtime fallback when instability detected
Risk: telemetry volume increases. Mitigation: sampling policy and aggregated rollups in console
qa_plan: Unit tests for flavor table lookup and KV tagging
End-to-end integration test harness with replayed production traces to validate stability and cost metrics
Canary rollout to non-sensitive tenants with feature flag; monitor latency, error rate, and quality metrics for 48h before wider rollout
